author: cnash03

text:
I'd use **hooks** for the tracking, plus a skill to write the summary. Here's why.

## Why not just a skill or an agent?
Skills and subagents only run when someone calls them. If you or your partner forget to type `/log-ai`, that session never gets recorded. For tracking that has to happen every time, you need **hooks**. Claude Code runs hooks itself on events like "user sent a prompt" or "Claude edited a file," so it doesn't depend on anyone remembering.

## Recommended setup

**1. Hooks capture the raw data (automatic).**
Put them in `.claude/settings.json` in the repo and commit it. Your partner then gets the same tracking as soon as they pull.
- `UserPromptSubmit` logs each prompt with the timestamp, git user and session ID.
- `PostToolUse` (on Edit/Write) logs which files Claude changed.
- `SessionEnd` saves a session summary or a copy of the transcript.

Write the logs to **one file per person per session**, e.g. `docs/ai-log/raw/<git-user>/<session-id>.jsonl`. If you both append to one shared file, you'll get merge conflicts all the time.

**2. A skill turns the logs into documentation (on demand).**
A `/ai-report` skill would read the raw logs and the git history, then write or update a readable `docs/AI_USAGE.md`. It would say who used AI, when, for what, which files it touched, and what was accepted or changed by hand. Run it before each milestone or submission.

**3. Commit trailers as a backup record.**
Claude already adds `Co-Authored-By: Claude` to the commits it makes. That gives you a second record in git history that the report can cross-check.

## Limits to know about
- **This only captures Claude Code.** If either of you uses ChatGPT, Copilot or Claude in the browser, the hooks won't see it. Add a short manual-entry section to `AI_USAGE.md`, or have the skill ask you about it.
- **Privacy:** raw prompts can include things you'd rather not commit. You can gitignore `raw/` and commit only the generated report.
- **Requirements:** your partner needs `jq` installed and has to be using Claude Code in this repo.

Want me to set this up? I'd add the hook script, `.claude/settings.json`, the `/ai-report` skill and a starter `docs/AI_USAGE.md`. Also tell me if your course has a required format for AI disclosure, and I'll make the report match it.

text:
Automatic AI-usage tracking is set up, and your planning-agent session is already written up as the first entry. I tested the logging with fake events (it hides API keys) and imported the planning session. Hooks are already logging this session. Nothing is committed yet.

**How it works**
- **Tracking is automatic.** Hooks in `.claude/settings.json` run the script `.claude/hooks/ai-log.sh` on every prompt, tool call, reply and multiple-choice decision. Each person's sessions go into their own folder, `docs/ai-log/raw/<git-user>/`, so you and your partner won't get merge conflicts. Your partner is tracked as soon as they pull and use Claude Code in the repo, as long as they have `jq` installed.
- **`/ai-report` writes the documentation.** It turns the logs into new entries in `docs/prompt-log.md` and rewrites `docs/AI_USAGE.md`. Anything only a person knows (whether it worked, what you changed) it asks as multiple choice, so you don't have to type. Run it after each phase or PR.
- **`AI_USAGE.md` follows the professor's criteria.** It has sections on the decisions you made, what the AI got wrong, how you pushed the tools, and what you don't let AI decide. Every claim points to a session ID. I checked the planning session's history to make sure it doesn't overclaim.

**The planning agent**
I took "add that as well" to mean document it. I imported its session (`be960576`) and wrote it up with your answers. The strongest evidence it gives you:
- **You overrode the AI.** It recommended a Blazor Web App and you chose MAUI because the team knows .NET.
- **The AI caught an error in your slides.** The mockup shows $1,231.50 of tax, but the IRS Tax Table gives about $1,235. You'll need to fix the demo numbers.
- **It went to primary sources.** It pulled the 2026 and 2027 tax numbers straight from the IRS Rev. Procs, released after the model's training cutoff.
- **It's honest about limits.** All tax numbers need a human check, and it read your "2026 and 2026" typo as 2026 and 2027 without asking.

**Other changes**
- **`BUILD_PLAN.md`:** the execution agent now runs `/ai-report` at the end of each phase instead of writing log entries by hand.
- **`README.md`:** a new section tells your partner how to set this up.
- **This session:** imported too, so the logging setup itself shows up in the next report.

**Limits**
- **Other tools aren't captured.** ChatGPT, Copilot and Claude on the web aren't logged automatically; `/ai-report` asks about them.
- **Raw prompts get committed.** That's how both of your reports see the whole team's sessions. Keys are hidden, but anything else you type is saved.
- **On Windows,** your partner needs Git Bash and `jq`.

Want me to commit all of this to a branch? If you meant something else by "add the planning agent," like a reusable planner agent file you can call again, I can add that too.
